title: From Grid Microphysics to the Radial Acceleration Relation: A Minimal Gradient-Coupled Excitation Model
abstract: A precise structural gap exists in Energy-Flow Cosmology: the covariant EFT requires a gravitational enhancement function mu(g) = 1/(exp(sqrt(g/a0))-1) that is formally identical to a Bose-Einstein occupation number, but this form cannot be derived from any classical local Lagrangian. We show that a minimal microscopic model — discrete degrees of freedom on a substrate (grid) with gradient-coupled excitation energy E proportional to sqrt(|nabla Phi|) — reproduces the observed functional form without free parameters beyond the measured scale a0. The key physical input is that excitation energy couples to local gravitational strain (gradient of the potential) rather than to the potential itself or to the density.

problem.identified_gap: Classical local Lagrangian cannot produce Bose-Einstein form of mu(g)
problem.obstruction: Classical action with finitely many derivatives produces polynomial corrections, not exponential suppression

three_assumptions.name: Bosonic statistics
three_assumptions.content: Excitation modes at each grid node obey Bose-Einstein statistics: <n> = 1/(exp(E/k_B T_grid) - 1)
three_assumptions.justification: Standard for non-interacting bosons; requires only discrete, indistinguishable modes

three_assumptions.name: Gradient-coupled excitation energy
three_assumptions.content: E(x) = hbar * omega_0 * sqrt(|nabla Phi(x)| / g*)
three_assumptions.justification: Node energy responds to local strain (gradient of potential), not potential itself or density

three_assumptions.name: Single scale
three_assumptions.content: a0 = g* * (k_B T_grid / hbar omega_0)^2 = 1.2e-10 m/s^2
three_assumptions.justification: Measured SPARC value; combines grid parameters into single observable

steps: Substitute E = hbar*omega_0*sqrt(g/g*) into BE distribution
Use a0 = g*(k_B T_grid / hbar omega_0)^2
derivation_chain.complete_chain: Grid DOF -> gradient coupling -> E proportional to sqrt(g) -> BE statistics -> mu(g) -> G_eff -> RAR

lattice_derivation.title: Lattice derivation of E proportional to sqrt(g)
lattice_derivation.setup: Two adjacent grid nodes i,j separated by l_g in gravitational field with local acceleration g
lattice_derivation.restoring_force: Delta F = -(nabla^2 Phi) * xi approx -(g/l_g) * xi (Hooke's law)
lattice_derivation.energy: E = hbar * omega proportional to sqrt(g)
lattice_derivation.robustness: Generic for any system where restoring force depends on local gradient of external potential

why_sqrt_g.gradient_coupling: In elastic medium, energy is proportional to strain; for discrete substrate in gravitational field, strain is |nabla Phi| * l_g

alternatives_fail.density_rho: Gives m_eff proportional to sqrt(G*rho); not a function of g alone, wrong functional form
alternatives_fail.potential_Phi: Gives m_eff proportional to sqrt(|Phi|); r-dependent, not universal
alternatives_fail.acceleration_g: Gives E proportional to sqrt(g); produces BE form with one universal scale a0

why_sqrt_g.conclusion: Only gradient coupling is consistent with observed universality of the RAR

eft_bridge.macro_framework: Covariant EFT establishes G_eff(g) = G_N(1 + mu(g)) with five structural properties for any decreasing mu(g)
eft_bridge.micro_model: Present note supplies the specific form of mu from gradient-coupled bosonic excitations
eft_bridge.complete_chain_eq14: Grid DOF -> E proportional to sqrt(g) -> mu(g) -> G_eff -> RAR

kt3_resolution.problem: KT3 gives beta=0.29 vs expected 0.50; transition radius dominated by bulk Lambda-scale
kt3_resolution.diagnosis: Classical discrete operator imposes bulk scale instead of local gradient scale
kt3_resolution.prediction: Statistical occupation (rather than classical field values) should restore beta=0.5
kt3_resolution.mechanism: Condition <n> ~ 1 gives g_trans ~ a0, therefore r_trans ~ sqrt(GM/a0) (MOND scaling)

limitations: No grid topology assumed (generic discrete bosonic modes)
No quantum field theory (BE used as input, not derived from path integral)
No derivation of a0 (measured, not predicted)

falsification_conditions.condition: mu must have exact BE form, not Fermi-Dirac, not classical Boltzmann, not power law
falsification_conditions.threshold: Deviation from BE form at ≤5% level (galaxy-survey precision)

falsification_conditions.condition: Coupling variable must be g = |nabla Phi|, not rho, Phi, or any other local quantity
falsification_conditions.test: Observational evidence for density-dependent or potential-dependent mu would falsify

falsification_conditions.condition: Excitation energy must scale as sqrt(g), i.e. E proportional to g^alpha with alpha = 1/2
falsification_conditions.test: Grid Hamiltonian derivation yielding alpha != 1/2 would falsify

falsification_conditions.condition: KT3 should recover beta = 0.5 when Graph-AQUAL incorporates statistical occupation
falsification_conditions.test: Concrete numerical test within existing GRAV pipeline
